title: John Lennon’s US deportation is overturned | 1975
content:
On 7 October 1975 the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit ruled in favour of John Lennon’s appeal to have his deportation ruling overturned.

On 4 September the court had heard arguments from both sides in the case of John Winston Ono Lennon v. Immigration and Naturalization Service. Chief Judge Irving R. Kaufman reserved his decision on Lennon’s efforts to gain US citizenship until this day.

Although Judge William H Mulligan rejected the request, Kaufman and Circuit Judge Murray I Gurfein both approved it, giving a 2:1 result in Lennon’s favour. It paved the way for Lennon to be finally given his coveted Green Card, granting him the right to live and work permanently in the US.

If, in our 200 years of independence, we have in some measure realized our ideals, it is in large part because we have always found a place for those committed to the spirit of liberty and willing to implement it. Lennon’s four-year battle to remain in our country is testimony to his faith in this American dream.
US Court of Appeals
